title: Constant curve assertions assemble over a finite clopen partition
statement: Let Λ be an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring, k an algebraically closed field, f : X → Spec k a separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most one [def-sc-curves], and M a Λ-module. Suppose a finite family of pairwise disjoint clopen opens U_i covers X. If the constant M sheaf on each U_i satisfies the eight assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] relative to U_i → X → Spec k, then the constant M sheaf on X satisfies all eight assertions. No smoothness, connectedness, finiteness or prime-annihilation hypothesis on M is imposed.

proof.text: A finite disjoint clopen cover realizes X as the coproduct of the pieces: morphisms from X glue uniquely from the disjoint opens, with no overlap compatibility. The existing clopen sheaf product theorem identifies abelian sheaves and global sections with the componentwise product. Constant sheaves restrict to the same constant module by upperStarConstantSheafIso, and forgetting coefficients preserves these isomorphisms.

Apply the existing finiteCoproductCohomologyAssembly to the underlying abelian sheaf and the clopen coproduct cofan. It identifies its cohomology with the product of the inverse-image cohomology on the pieces. Normalize those restrictions by the constant-sheaf isomorphisms. Equivalently, exact finite direct image along the clopen inclusions gives the same identification by the edge maps.

Affineness and properness restrict to closed components. Constructibility restricts to open subschemes. The geometric-stalk formula for inverse image restricts primary and invertible-order torsion. Apply the supplied component assertions to obtain C1-C5.

Pull a field-extension square or an open immersion back to every clopen piece. Finite base change and naturality identify each cohomology comparison with the finite product of the component comparisons. Products of bijective maps are bijective and finite products of surjective maps are surjective. This yields C6-C8. An empty index forces X to be empty and gives zero cohomology; a singleton is the identity case.

theorem assertions_constant_of_isClopen (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)
    {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsClosed (U i : Set X))
    (hdisj : Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (U i : Set X) (U j)))
    (hcov : ∀ x : X, ∃ i, x ∈ U i)
    (H : ∀ i, Assertions Λ ((U i).ι ≫ f)
      ((constantSheaf (U i).toScheme.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M)) :
    Assertions Λ f ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M)
